text: An OpenSearch Service software update: a new release of the service's own software for the domain (releases ending in `-P` and a number are patches). It is not an engine version upgrade. Required updates generally carry critical security fixes; most updates are optional.

This cannot be expressed in code. Terraform, CloudFormation and CDK can only switch automatic software updates on (`auto_software_update_enabled`, `SoftwareUpdateOptions`, `enableAutoSoftwareUpdate`) and set the off-peak window; none can apply a given release. The engine version in code does not change.
A CVE is named here only when an AWS security bulletin names this service software release. AWS's examples of required updates are Log4j CVEs and enforcing IMDSv2.

Service software updates use a blue/green deployment: the domain stays available while the node count temporarily rises, often doubling, with possible higher latency and rejected requests, and extra load on dedicated master nodes. Updates typically complete within minutes and can take hours or days under heavy load.

An optional update is never forced. A required update is installed by AWS in the off-peak window once its deadline passes. AWS's current pages state the deadline two ways (typically 14 days from availability, and a 30-day rule); the date on this card is the one the API returned for this domain. AWS also states that a domain left without a required update is first isolated (all network access removed) and later permanently deleted with its data.
The person running this needs `es:DescribeDomain`, `es:StartServiceSoftwareUpdate` and `es:CancelServiceSoftwareUpdate` on this domain.

Read the update's state in `ServiceSoftwareOptions` (`UpdateAvailable`, `NewVersion`, `OptionalDeployment`, `AutomatedUpdateDate`). A domain that is processing a change, has a red cluster status, a high error rate or split brain is not eligible. Check there is headroom for the temporary extra nodes.
OpenSearch Service takes hourly automated snapshots. Take a manual snapshot to a repository you control if you need a restore point of your own.
OpenSearch Service console, Region {region} > Domains > select `{id}` > Actions > Update > choose Apply update now or Schedule it in off-peak window > Confirm.
Schedule the update for the domain's off-peak window.
Or start the update now, outside the off-peak window.
`UpdateStatus` goes from `PENDING_UPDATE` to `IN_PROGRESS` to `COMPLETED` and `CurrentVersion` becomes the new release. Check the cluster is green.

An update can be cancelled only in the `PENDING_UPDATE` state. For updates applied on or after April 24, 2026 a rollback is supported for 15 days, once per update, unless a configuration change was made after the update, AWS applied a mandatory update after its deadline, or the update rode along with another blue/green change.

By default any change to the domain that causes a blue/green deployment (instance type, security groups, advanced settings and others) also installs the latest service software (`UseLatestServiceSoftwareForBlueGreen`), and an update installed that way can't be rolled back. An unrelated infrastructure change can therefore apply this update.
An engine version upgrade of the domain (OpenSearch or Elasticsearch version). The in-place upgrade runs as a blue/green deployment and can't be paused, cancelled or rolled back.
This has a code equivalent: the engine version of the domain (`OpenSearch_X.Y` or `Elasticsearch_X.Y`).

Change `engine_version` on the `aws_opensearch_domain` (`OpenSearch_X.Y` or `Elasticsearch_X.Y`). The provider documentation does not say whether this is an in-place upgrade or a replacement: read the plan before merging, and stop if it says the domain must be replaced.

The provider documents these as forcing a new domain: adding or removing `vpc_options`, and `advanced_security_options.enabled` going from true to false. CoderHelm also refuses a change to `domain_name` in an upgrade change.

Change `EngineVersion` on the `AWS::OpenSearchService::Domain`, and only with the `UpdatePolicy: EnableVersionUpgrade: true` attribute on the resource. With the policy the version updates without replacement.

Without `UpdatePolicy: EnableVersionUpgrade: true` (or with it false), changing `EngineVersion` makes CloudFormation replace the whole domain: a new empty domain is created and the old one is deleted with its data. The policy must be on the resource before, or in the same change as, the version change. `DomainName` and `EngineMode` are replacement properties, changing `EncryptionAtRestOptions` re-creates the domain, and switching `AWS::Elasticsearch::Domain` to `AWS::OpenSearchService::Domain` in a template deletes the domain.

Change the `version` of the `opensearchservice.Domain`, and only with `enableVersionUpgrade: true` on the domain (it defaults to false). On an L1 `CfnDomain`, set `cfnOptions.updatePolicy = { enableVersionUpgrade: true }`.

`enableVersionUpgrade` defaults to false, and without it a version change replaces the whole domain with an empty one. Changing a construct id or the domain name replaces it too. The default `removalPolicy` is RETAIN.
The upgrade takes from 15 minutes to several hours. The domain stays available, write performance can degrade, and OpenSearch Dashboards might be unavailable for some or all of it.

Check the upgrade path is supported (OpenSearch 1.3 or 2.x must reach 2.19 before 3.x; indexes created on old versions may need reindexing first). The service runs pre-upgrade checks and does not proceed unless they pass: green cluster, disk usage below 90%, JVM memory pressure below 75%, fewer than 1,000 shards per node, no snapshot in progress, plugins available on the target. With managed disaster recovery, upgrade the secondary domain first.
Take a manual snapshot before upgrading. The service takes its own pre-upgrade snapshot and uses it only to restore the cluster if the upgrade fails.

An in-place engine upgrade can't be rolled back. To return to the earlier version, restore a manual snapshot on a new domain. Snapshots taken on OpenSearch 1.x and Elasticsearch 7.10 or earlier are incompatible with OpenSearch 3.x.
